people.gloss: The good rain that knows its season (Đỗ Phủ: hảo vũ tri thời tiết)
people.role: Abbess of Cốc Vũ Quán since 958: rain-calling rites and spirit-rice terraces for the farmers of the south
people.appearance: A small, brown, smiling woman in a patched grey robe and a rice-straw hat, with mud to the knee and a cough she hides in her sleeve.
people.backstory: Dương Hảo Vũ was born in 830 in a drought year at Phong Đăng, to tenants on the Lục family's farms, whose harvests the Tower taxes first (A288). The abbey's rain came the week she was born, and her mother named her for it. She went up the bamboo hill at ten. The founder Hạng Đảo Vũ (hang_dao_vu) was a rain priestess from the coast who called rain with Water, and by then the hill had stopped answering her. When the founder died in 958, Dương became abbess. She spent forty years learning to call rain the other way: not from the sea, but from the forest's own breath (N-coc_vu-02). It worked, and the farmers have had their rain since. In the great drought of 1150 she held the Grain Rain rite for nine days over the valleys of Phong Đăng and Ương Ca. Her meridians have not been right since. Every autumn she sends rice to Thu Phần's singers and asks them to sing more softly. Their founder, Lý Hận Bích (ly_han_bich), was born the same year as she was, and wants the opposite thing for the dead.
people.wants: Rain for every planting and no rain sold; and the dead of Lôi Trạch at rest before she is.
people.secret: Since 1010 the prior has sold the abbey's rain to the Night Rain Market in dry years, and since 1150 the pills that keep her meridians open have been bought with that money. She knows both things, and she has never asked.

people.role: Prior (giám viện) of the abbey: its stores, its tax, and the rain it sells in dry years
people.appearance: A plump, pleasant monk with an abacus in his sleeve and the soft hands of a man who keeps the books.
people.backstory: A rice merchant's son from Thu Trì who came to the abbey at twenty and never quite stopped counting. Since 1010 he has sold the abbey's rain to Kiều Mãn Lâu (kieu_man_lau) in dry years, so that the Night Rain Market can open, and recorded a third of the price. The rest buys the pills that keep the abbess (duong_hao_vu) breathing. He thinks he is the only one who knows.

people.backstory: The third son of the Lục family, whose harvests at Phong Đăng the Tower taxes first (A288). He gave up the farms for the terraces at twenty, and the spirit rice of the abbey is better for it. His family's tenants send their children to the Tower's Bell Test first and to him when they fail, as the Thiều boy came. He does not mind being second.

people.backstory: Born in Yên Vũ Trấn, the town of misty rain, she has the best rain hands in the abbey. In dry years the prior Thời Tri Tiết (thoi_tri_tiet) sends her to Thu Trì to call rain at dusk so that Kiều Mãn Lâu's (kieu_man_lau) market can open, and she stays to drink in it. She has stopped asking what the rain is for.

people.role: Founder of Cốc Vũ Quán (610): a coast rain priestess who called rain with Water
people.backstory: A rain priestess from the sea-spray coast who came inland in a drought and founded the abbey on a bamboo hill above Phong Đăng to call the rain for the farmers and grow spirit rice (V154). She called rain from the sea with Water, and it came for three hundred years. The hill held no Water of its own, and it came less each century. She died in 958, in a dry year, under the last rain she called. Her disciple Dương Hảo Vũ (duong_hao_vu) learned to call it from the forest instead.

ties.note: her successor
